links.comparator_used: Self-reported (verbalized) confidence metrics (first and mean self-reported confidence), plus consistency-based metrics alone (relative entropy, majority-vote percentage)
links.outcome: Discrimination of correct vs incorrect answers (ROC AUC), Spearman correlation of confidence with accuracy, and calibration (ECE, Brier score)
links.effect: Top Weighted Score (hybrid of response frequency and self-reported confidence) was the only metric with significant correlations across all 4 models: Gemini-3-Pro ρ=0.52, GPT-5 ρ=0.43, Claude-4.5-Sonnet ρ=0.30, GPT-4o ρ=0.22. AUC 0.826 (95% CI 0.731-0.920) for Gemini-3-Pro and 0.767 (95% CI 0.668-0.866) for GPT-5. Lowest ECE in GPT-5 (0.098) and Claude-4.5-Sonnet (0.192); Gemini-3-Pro was comparable between relative entropy (0.119) and Top Weighted Score (0.122). It was the only significant metric in GPT-4o.
links.tradeoff: Consistency-based and hybrid metrics need 20 repeated outputs per case. Reasoning models required substantially longer processing times and higher token consumption than the general model. The authors call for resource-efficient sampling strategies, and association strength varied across models.
links.quote: Receiver operating characteristic analysis revealed that Top Weighted Score demonstrated the highest discriminative ability, with area under the curve values of 0.826 (95% CI 0.731-0.920) for Gemini-3-Pro and 0.767 (95% CI 0.668-0.866) for GPT-5.
